newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MKT GREETS KARAMANLIS' WIN, AWAITS POLICY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK MKT GREETS KARAMANLIS' WIN, AWAITS POLICY.

text.p: Greek markets welcomed the election of Costas Karamanlis to the helm of the conservative opposition New Democracy party but waited to see what kind of economic policies the party will espouse before rendering judgement.

"It is certainly a positive development to see a young politician leading a major Greek political party and it is up to him to shift the party away from the populist economic policies of his predecessor," said the head of sales at an international brokerage.
Karamanlis, a lawyer, 41, beat former conservative economy minister George Souflias, his main opponent, and party president Miltiadis Evert at a party congress on Friday night.
Evert lost the general elections to socialist Premier Costas Simitis last September.

Karamanlis should manage to unite his party, pick competent people to advise him and help formulate a market-oriented economic policy devoid of populism that addresses the country's economic problems, said the manager who requested anonymity.
New Democracy is badly divided and disoriented following an election loss last September to the ruling PASOK socialist party.

"If the past is a good indicator for the future, then his political inexperience and youth could well turn out to be an asset instead of a liability," said a banker. "We have seen the results of policies pursued by experienced, old politicians."
Bankers said it was too early to judge the impact of Karamanlis' election on the market but they saw benefits with the political pendulum swinging towards the centre.

"It is too early to assess the market impact of his election," said Harris Makkas, deputy general manager at Bank of America."But it should be positive in the medium-term because it swings the pendulum to the centre and more prudent economic policies."
Karamanlis has to be explicit in his articulation of economic policy in order to reclaim part of the political centre that has been conceded to the socialists, said Makkas.

"The centre is going to be the new battle ground and Prime Minister Costas Simitis will have to bring his economic policies closer to the centre to fend off a likely challenge by Karamanlis," he said. "This should be good news for the economy."
Other bankers also said it was too early to render judgement on Karamanlis.
"It is too early to say anything," said Mike Paparis, treasurer at Midland Bank. "We have more than three years to go before the next general elections will be held."
But some bankers and brokers warned against repeating past mistakes that sent conservative voters into the Simitis' socialist fold.

"He (Karamanlis) should know that sticking to the traditional pro-state economic policies espoused by New Democracy in the recent past will cost him in the next national elections," said a senior banker who requested anonymity.
He added that the message, the messenger and the medium should be in harmony with the needs of a modern economy and society.

"New Democracy should embark on a radical change of economic policy," he said. "This means not just a new, young leader at the party helm but also new faces without previous involvement in party politics and infighting coupled with fresh ideas." -- Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
